cleared.title: Thread pool with no per-solver timeout or cancellation
cleared.evidence: with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(solvers)) as pool: ... fut.result()  # no blocking timeout; each solver runs unbounded
cleared.recommendation: Add a per-solver timeout (e.g., 60s) via pool.submit(fn, timeout=60) or wrap fut.result() in a timeout guard. Without this, a hung or deadlocked solver blocks the entire intake and consumes a thread slot permanently.

cleared.title: No cooldown or dedup between solver retries / re-runs
cleared.evidence: run_intake iterates solvers once; there is no guard against re-running intake rapidly, no back-off, and no dedup of identical failure patterns. In production, a transient API outage could cause repeated immediate re-runs, flooding logs and consuming API quota.
cleared.recommendation: Add a module-level cooldown (e.g., 60s) or a simple file-based lock that prevents re-entry within a window. Also record the last-run timestamp in intake.json and surface it in the CLI so operators can see throttle state.

findings.title: Thread pool shutdown may cancel pending solver results on timeout
findings.evidence: pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) in run_intake will cancel futures that have not yet completed, even those still pending within their individual deadline. If a solver is in the middle of a legitimate but slow response (e.g., 200s into a 300s timeout), it will be killed abruptly rather than allowed to finish naturally.
findings.recommendation: Consider using wait=False without cancel_futures, or only cancel futures that have exceeded the deadline, to allow in-progress solvers to complete if they are within their allowed window.

findings.title: Potential double-truncation of report when context capping interacts with MAX_REPORT_CHARS
findings.evidence: The _prepare function first caps the report via _cap(report, MAX_REPORT_CHARS) and then builds the prompt via build_solver_prompt which also caps individual context files against MAX_TOTAL_CONTEXT_CHARS. If a report is exactly at the 60000-char boundary and contexts push the total over 120000, the initial _cap may have already truncated text that later context capping removes from the total count,
findings.recommendation: Review the flow: ensure the report capping and context total capping are coordinated, or that a second cap on the final prompt is intentional and documented.
